To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the brain's response to a stressor is organized by two complementary modes of operation of the stress system, one fast and one slow.

The stress system orchestrating the body's response to environmental challenges consists of two modes of operation that are mediated by corticotropineleasing hormone (CRF), the urocortin family of peptides and the two corticosteroid receptors, the mineralocorticoid (MR) and the glucocorticoid (GR) receptors.
the brain's stress system is organized in two distinct modes, a fast and a slower mode.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the understanding of the mechanisms by which stress hormones and their receptors act in the brain to control stress responses and behaviour, and the implications of this knowledge for stress-related disorders and the development of novel therapeutic strategies.
the elucidation of the molecular mechanisms underlying the actions of stress mediators on brain and behaviour.
the elucidation of the mechanisms by which glucocorticoid hormones and their receptors regulate stress responses, and how these mechanisms may be altered in stress-related disorders.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the stress system is a brain-body axis that is essential for adaptation, survival, health and disease.
the stress system orchestrates the body and brain responses and that this is essential for health and disease. (C) 2010 Elsevier B.V. All
the stress system is a key player for the maintenance of health.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the stress system is the brain's interface to the body and the body's interface to the brain.
stress system dysregulation is a common denominator for many psychiatric diseases.
stress is a normal and adaptive response of the brain and body to environmental challenge, which becomes pathological when the stress response is not switched off.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a balanced activity of the stress system is essential for mental and physical health.
the stress system is a dynamic system that can be manipulated to improve the balance between the two stress system operation modes.
stress is a normal part of life and the stress system is essential to maintain homeostasis.
